prose: In Episode 20 of Inner Whirled, we take on one of the least known revelations of biblical astro-theology: that Miriam of Exodus and Mary of the New Testament are the same archetypal character, proven by celestial symbolism and linguistic forensics.
Drawing on the work of Reverend Robert Taylor, we once again demonstrate how biblical narratives function as astronomical allegories, and how those who taught this in prior centuries were persecuted.
topics: Miriam = Mary: symbolic and linguistic connections
Virgo and Venus as the “Divine Feminine” archetype
The Red Sea as astronomical allegory
Reverend Robert Taylor and persecution for astro-theology
Media, control, and the shaping of belief systems
ext: We move from connection into code. The Exodus account unfolds as a sky map where Virgo, Venus, and the Red Sea aren’t metaphors, but coordinates. From the rising and falling of constellations to “persecution” as celestial following, we trace a system far older than scripture.
